newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ short rates nudge lower, yields higher at close.
newsitem.headline: NZ short rates nudge lower, yields higher at close.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD
OVERNIGHT CASH 8.15 PCT (PREV 8.20) US 5-YR 6.10 (PREV 6.10)
* NZ 90-days end on opening levels, yields creep higher
* Market consolidating after new government
* All eyes on Reserve Bank statement on Tuesday
New Zealand's money markets ended on their opening levels on Friday after a very quiet session, while bond yields nudged higher once more.
Ninety-day bank bills were steady at 7.90 percent, three basis points below Thursday's close. The front futures contract was down three at 92.79.
Meanwhile, mid bonds ended the week four basis points weaker while the long bond was off seven at 7.40 percent.
Bill dealers said the market remained very well bid but was consolidating its position after an extremely bulled up day on Wednesday following the formation of a new centre-right government.
Many were busy trying to digest the new government's policies, especially the implications for the economy of a rise in government spending.
Traders were also looking ahead to the Reserve Bank's monetary policy statement on Tuesday and had taken a bullish view, with most risk seen on the downside.
One dealer said that in the new 0-3 percent inflation environment, she could easily see 90-day bill rates at 7.80 percent.

"The question is whether they are going to go to 7.50 percent. I see that as definitely a cut-off -- I don't think the Reserve Bank would be particularly happy with them lower than there, with increased spending and the last CPI (consumers price index) up close to that three percent band anyway."
The dealer saw the RBNZ as content with 90-day bills at eight percent and the currency's Trade-Weighted Index at 66.5.
